items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:27PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A strong front moves toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight
tonight. Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled with
a lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2 feet
above normal high tide late tonight into early Thursday morning.
Strongest winds are expected to peak Thursday morning, with up to
0.5 inches of rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are
perpendicular to the southerly wind direction, such as
Kwigillingok, have a higher chance of seeing impacts with this
f

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move in Wednesday evening, with moderate to heavy rain and
gusty winds expected through Thursday. Rainfall totals are
expected to be around 1 to 1.50 inches, with wind gusts up to 55
mph out of the east/southeast.

* WHERE...St. Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...Wednesday September 2 through Thursday September 3.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain and gusty winds could make travel difficult
at times.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 2 at 2:06PM AKDT until September 5 at 11:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels 2.0 to 4.0 feet above the normal high tide
line.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast and Eastern Norton Sound
Coast from Golovin to Stebbins.

* WHEN...From 10 PM Thursday to 11 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels are expected to peak early
Friday morning during the time of high tide. While water levels
will subside somewhat later Friday, a second rise is expected
during the Saturday morning high tide
items.areas: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Frost Advisory issued September 2 at 12:12PM AKDT until September 3 at 8:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 32 will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...City and Borough of Yakutat.

* WHEN...From 2 AM to 8 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
items.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. Sensitive
plants and shrubs should be covered or brought indoors if possible.
